title: Add the Agent run block to the timeline

session.words: Reading of the ask: (1) set up a workspace with a git repo for this project's work. No repos are attached yet; check list_repos for a suitable one (e.g. agent_os/agents_os). If none exists, init a local git repo in the workspace and ask Andrei to create a GitHub repo so you can attach and push. (2) Publish an HTML artifact that's otherwise empty and holds the user's JSON, exactly as given in the m
session.why: The session started on 2026-10-24. Its goal is to build the Agent OS page. The page is an artifact. It runs from its JSON state.

run.why: Andrei sent a drawing for the timeline. After each run, the timeline must show an Agent run block. When you select the block, it shows only the timeline of this agent. This timeline shows the start and the steps, for example "finding..." and "creating file". It also shows the subagents, the MCP uses, the skill uses and the workflows. Then the block shows the Details: what started the session, the run, the workflow, the subagent and the skill. Then it shows the files that the agent read (had in context), updated, deleted or created. Each file shows its context size, if it is in the cached context, and why. After each run, a subagent or a workflow makes a run.json from the run logs. It puts the run.json into the state. When the page starts or refreshes, the timeline shows the last run first.

subagents.name: run-recorder (general-purpose)
subagents.why: The main agent started it at the end of the run. It records this run in runs/<session>-<run>.json from the session log. The timeline shows this file as an Agent run block.
